citation: Thondre PS, Young E, Pledger S et al. (2026). A randomized controlled trial in healthy participants to compare the insulinogenic effects of whey protein and pea protein co-ingested with glucose. PLOS One 21(1):e0340386.
protocol: Five drinks, single-blind crossover: 50 g glucose alone; + 10 or 20 g pea protein (8/16 g protein); + 10 or 20 g whey protein concentrate (8.1/16.2 g protein); fat 0.6-1.8 g. Capillary glucose and plasma insulin at -5, 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180 min.
population: n=30 healthy adults, age 31.1 ± 10.0 y, BMI 23.2 ± 2.8 kg/m2 (Table 2, mean ± SD).

reports.where: Table 3: iAUC at 60, 90, 120, 180 min, peak and time of peak per drink
Table 4: iAUC at 60, 90, 120, 180 min, peak and time of peak per drink, µU/mL·min

note: Paired-meal contrast, protein_source: glucose + pea protein vs glucose + whey at two matched protein doses. Two-dose plant against animal design on a fixed glucose load, so it also gives a protein-dose effect. Watch: sex split not in the table, glucose is capillary. Only in figures: glucose and insulin time courses.
